thread:
Maya: Quick flag 0 min ago I hit a bad onboarding UX in the Python sample app. The API returned 401 but the SDK bubbled up 'Request failed' and no actionable hint. New devs are getting stuck.
Sam: Ugh. Is that the same flow where the token-refresh path swallows the original status?
Maya: Exactly. The transport logs show 401 with JSON body explaining key expired, but the exception shown to app is opaque.
Jordan: Node and Go SDKs have an AuthError class that surfaces status and a small metadata map. Looks like py isn't consistent.
Li: From product POV we should show a CTA in the sample app when auth fails ("Re-run `ri login`"). Otherwise folks open support tickets.
Sam: Developer proposal: standardize SDK exception taxonomy across languages: AuthError, RateLimitError, ClientError, ServerError, TransportError. Each exception carries: "status", "retryable" (bool), "retry_after" (string|null), "hint" (string|null).
Jordan: Also: do not rewrite 4xx into 5xx classes. Keep original status so callers can branch.
Maya: Can we also include a machine-readable code, e.g., "code": "auth.invalid_token"? That helps programmatic handling in sample apps.
Sam: I like code, but keep it as a short string (no nested objects). We'll add it to metadata.
Li: Docs should show mapping examples: when to show CTA vs. when to surface a retry banner. UX wants a short, imperative copy in "hint" (e.g., "Run `ri login` to refresh credentials.").
Jordan: Implementing checklist:
- runtime: confirm status codes for auth/ratelimit (ENG-RUNTIME)
- py-sdk: expose typed exceptions + metadata + parse Retry-After
- node/go: add unit tests asserting parity
- sample-app: show hint + CTA for AuthError and RateLimitError
- telemetry: add error_class tag for onboarding funnel
Sam: I'll take the py change. Plan: add exceptions module, map http statuses at the transport layer before raising, include response headers in metadata. ETA: 3 workdays.
Maya: Great. Jordan, can you own parity tests? Quick test matrix: status -> exception class, metadata keys present, retry_after parsed when header present.
Jordan: Yep. I'll add a test runner job in CI that runs the SDK parity suite on PRs touching sdk/* and sample-app.
Li: For sample-app copy I'll write small snippets and UX rules: prefer explicit CTAs, avoid raw JSON error dumps, keep one-sentence explanation + action.
Maya: One more concern: we occasionally leak transport stacks into user-facing logs. Let's make sure default exception.__str__ is friendly; include raw body only in debug mode.
Sam: Agree. We'll add a debug flag env var to include verbose error info.
error-bot: (automated) created ticket INF-4399: "SDK parity: typed exceptions + onboarding hints" assigned to sam.
Maya: Once py PR is draft, post link here and we'll run sample-app canary in staging.
Sam: Draft PR up: https://git.internal/redwood/py-sdk/pull/198 (draft). Comments welcome. :thumbsup:
Jordan: Reviewing. If tests pass, we can merge and coordinate staging deploy.
Maya: Thanks team. This should cut a bunch of onboarding noise and reduce support tickets.
